newsitem.title: FRANCE: FIGURE SKATING-ELTSOVA AND BUSHKOV TRIUMPH AGAIN.
newsitem.headline: FIGURE SKATING-ELTSOVA AND BUSHKOV TRIUMPH AGAIN.

text.p: Marina Eltsova and Andrei Bushkov survived an early mistake to add the European pairs figure skating title to their world crown on Wednesday night.
They captured their second European title with a clear victory in a high quality free skating battle against Germans Mandy Woetzel and Ingo Steuer, the champions two years ago.
The Russian couple, who won on their first appearance in 1993, looked to have thrown away their chance when Eltsova lost balance and touched one hand on the ice on their first jump, a triple loop.
But she picked herself up and they skated flawlessly for the rest of their routine.
"It did not come into our minds then that we might lose. If you have such thoughts you cannot skate at all. We just concentrated on our programme," Eltsova said of the error.
The Germans, who had beaten the Russian pair three times this season, were also excellent but could not overtake their rivals, losing on an 8-1 decision from the nine judges.
Steuer played down the Russians' mistake. "It was a little mistake, not important and they are good and worthy champions."
Russians Elena Berezhnaia and Anton Sikharulidze took the bronze, knocking Sarah Abitbol and Stephane Bernadis of France down to fourth.
Berezhnaia, 19, had a career-threatening accident when she was struck on the head by the skate of her former partner, Oleg Shliakov, during practice in December 1995.
She was in hospital for a month and still has a large scar on one side of her head.
She returned to the rink in March last year and linked up with Sikarulidze, 20.

Under the guidance of the renowned Tamara Moskvina they have progressed far in a short time. The two couples above them could come under further pressure from them at the world championships in Lausanne in March.
